result.of2_default_ruling: CORRECTLY SEPARATED AT THE MECHANICS, CONTRADICTORY AT THE PLANDOC FRAMING — two distinct layers must not be conflated. (1) The make_gpp_compile_fn signature default opt_flag=\"-O2\" is NOT the 'CEB default' that OF-2 governs; it is a transitional builder-signature fallback for the two unchanged callers (:226/:402). OF-2's 'CEB-Default = Ofast' lives on the PLANNER/XML layer, realized as DefaultOptLevelSubAxis = OptOfastSubAxis and hard-enforced by static_assert at optimization_level_sub_axis.hpp:128 (verified). These are different layers, so the -O2 signature default is NOT a contradiction with OF-2 — it is the CORRECT and REQUIRED choice for opt-b: changing it to 'Ofast' would immediately pull the unchanged callers to -Ofast, break the opt-b/opt-c separation and void opt-b's behavioral neutrality. opt-b must NOT touch the signature-default value. (2) HOWEVER, the plan's PROSE does not draw this layer distinction. BAUPLAN §3:23 and §6 TABU :50-51 frame -O2 as a STANDING/permanent architectural pin ('Default MUSS -O2 exakt reproduzieren', 'NIE auf -O3 kippen'), which DOES contradict OF-2 verbatim (Ledger:1924: 'nichts gepinnt, JEDES TEIL beweglich, keine Byte-Identitaet-Pin-Annahme mehr'). RULING: keep the C++ signature default -O2 exactly as SOLL specifies (correct); reframe/deprecate the permanent -O2 pin language to opt-b-local transitional and scope the byte-identity gate to opt-b isolation (must be corrected). The reconciliation is purely in the plan's rationale wording, not in the code.
